locked.say: Tab (Edit Mode) unlocks in Lesson 05. Hold that thought.

bites.title: The table of contents
bites.body: That panel on the right is the Outliner. It lists every object in your scene, even the ones you can't see. Think of it as the cast list.

bites.title: Point at a name
bites.body: Click Suzanne's name in the Outliner. She lights up in the viewport too. Two views, one selection.
bites.hint: Find the row with a little triangle icon named Suzanne and click the name.

bites.title: Name things
bites.body: Double-click the Light's name in the Outliner, type Sun, press Enter. Good names are a gift to future you.
bites.hint: Double-click the name text itself, not the icon. Or select it and press F2 over the viewport.

bites.title: Now you see it
bites.body: Click the eye icon on the Camera's row. It vanishes from the viewport but it's still in the scene, just napping.
bites.hint: Right edge of the Camera row: the little eye.

bites.title: Bring them all back
bites.body: Hover the viewport and press Alt+H. Everything hidden comes back at once. (H alone hides whatever is selected.)

bites.title: Family tree
bites.body: Click Suzanne, then Shift+click the cube so the cube is selected last. Press Ctrl+P and choose Object. The last one you click becomes the parent.
bites.hint: Order matters: Suzanne first, cube last (it gets the brighter outline). Then Ctrl+P, Object.

bites.title: Along for the ride
bites.body: Select just the cube and grab it with G. Suzanne rides along, because children follow their parents.

bites.title: Read the tree
bites.body: Look at the Outliner: Suzanne now lives indented under Cube. Click the little arrow beside Cube to fold and unfold the family.

bites.title: Boxes for things
bites.body: Select Suzanne, hover the viewport, press M, choose + New Collection, call it Props, click OK. Collections are folders for objects.
bites.hint: M opens Move to Collection. The + New Collection item is at the bottom.

bites.title: Lesson 03: cleared
bites.body:
You can find, rename, hide, parent, and file things. Big scenes won't scare you now.

Reward: the Properties editor just slid in under the Outliner. Every setting in Blender lives in there. Scroll on for Lesson 04.
